qwen/qwen3-235b-a22b-2507.mistake: The natural language sentence is logically equivalent to saying Daxton either does both (organizes community events and creates educational content), or neither. However, the FOL expression ¬ (p₁(Daxton) ⊕ p₁₂(Daxton)) correctly captures exactly that: the negation of exclusive or, meaning both or neither. The natural language sentence is a correct and clear paraphrase of the logical meaning. There is no mistake. Therefore, the mapping is correct.

openai/gpt-5-mini.mistake: Minor nuance in item 13: The FOL p_5(Daxton) → (p_6(Daxton) ⊕ p_7(Daxton)) asserts that if Daxton is passionate then exactly one of p_6 or p_7 is true (a hard exclusive deterministic claim). The NL wording "he can either start ... or inspire ..." can be read as expressing a possibility/option (may do one or the other) rather than a definite exclusive fact. If the intended reading of the NL was a firm exclusive outcome, the FOL is correct; if the NL intended only to express that those are possible alternatives, the FOL is stronger than the NL.
